=== CURRENT STATE (PATCH 9-10) — READ THIS FIRST ===
The primary evaluation policy is the SMOOTH severity-adaptive (SOFA-graded)
stochastic policy pi_e(EGDT|X)=expit(beta*(sofa-m)/s), defined in the

=== KEY DESIGN NOTE for ASR scoring ===
For the ASR conformal score, the prediction interval is
  [pred_y0 - rhat, pred_y0 + rhat]
so the point estimate is EXACTLY the interval midpoint. This means:
- The point estimate is the same for tCOPP-EIF(I), tCOPP-EIF(M),
  tCOPP-EIF(P) within Block B (they share the same outcome model;
  only the conformal cutoff rhat differs).
- The point estimate WILL differ between Block A's EIF(I) and Block B's
  EIF(M)/EIF(P) because they use different training subsets.
This is informative: the methods agree on the prediction, they only
disagree on the uncertainty.

=== PATCH 3 HOTFIX (Option C) — displayed point = interval midpoint ===
After running Patch 3 we observed that in Block A's tCOPP-W panels, the
displayed mu_hat dots sometimes fell visibly OUTSIDE the conformal error
bars. Cause: with bootstrap aggregation (BootSweight, B=20), the combined
interval is the majority-vote union of B per-iteration intervals and need
not be symmetric around the bootstrap-averaged mu_hat — particularly when
the per-iteration outcome model is unstable (Logistic on NE-only data,
~412 patients, 19 covariates). Block B's intervals didn't show this
because the federated/pooled cutoff is wider AND the outcome model
trains on more patients, making per-iteration predictions more stable.

Fix: in make_panel, the displayed black dot is now the INTERVAL MIDPOINT
(lwr + upr)/2 rather than mu_hat. By construction the dot is always
inside the bar, eliminating the visual confusion. mu_hat is still computed
and stored in upmcIntv for diagnostic use (e.g., calibration analysis).
The mu_col argument to make_panel is kept for backward compatibility but
no longer affects what's plotted.

=== PATCH 6 APPLIED — hard SOFA policy via splicing, B=1, hide point dot ===
Modifications to this file only (multisource_fixed_patch6.Rmd is unchanged
from patch5 except for the changelog header).

Per advisor meeting, three substantive changes:

(1) HIDE displayed point estimate. make_panel no longer draws the black
    midpoint dot. mu_hat is still computed inside the analysis functions
    and stored in upmcIntv as a diagnostic (and is still used internally
    for ranking patients within each panel; we just don't draw the dot).
    The mu_col argument is kept for backward compatibility but unused.

(2) BOOTSTRAP REMOVED. Each analysis block now uses B = 1 with method =
    "Sweight" instead of B = B_MS = 20 with "BootSweight". Single-split
    conformal: faster, simpler, and produces symmetric intervals
    [mu_hat - rhat, mu_hat + rhat] for ASR scoring (no asymmetric
    aggregation across bootstrap iterations). Conformal validity is
    unaffected — bootstrap aggregation reduces split-induced noise but
    isn't required for the coverage guarantee.

(3) HARD SOFA POLICY via splicing. Replace the soft pi_e in {0.1, 0.9}
    primary with a hard policy: pi_e(EGDT|X) = 1 if SOFA >= 4, else 0.
    Implemented by running BOTH constant-policy analyses (Deta_egdt and
    Deta_uc) and splicing per-patient based on sofa_high_idx. This avoids
    the variance inflation that the soft heterogeneous policy caused on
    the small Region 1 calibration sample, so EIF(I) intervals should be
    much tighter than under patch 5.

Each analysis block restructured:
  - First half: Deta <- Deta_egdt (was Deta_sofa). Saves to *_0 suffix.
  - Second half: previously wrapped in if(FALSE); now if(TRUE) so it
    actually runs Deta_uc. Saves to *_1 suffix.
  - Final upmcIntv data frame includes:
      * _egdt and _uc columns (raw counterfactual outputs, diagnostic)
      * _sofa columns (spliced from _0 / _1 by sofa_high_idx)
  - Plot chunks (unchanged) read _sofa columns -> SOFA-policy figures.

Runtime: each block runs analysis TWICE (once per Deta) -> ~2x patch4
on its own, but with B=1 instead of B=20 the net runtime is ~10x FASTER
than patch4 / patch5.

This is the last planned patch.

=== PATCH 7 APPLIED — code-quality cleanup, mostly no methodology change ===

Patch 7 is a code-quality pass on top of Patch 6. Most changes are purely
cosmetic / safety; ONE change has a real impact on the outcome model and
is flagged below. None of the changes alter the SOFA-thresholded policy,
the splicing logic, or the analysis pipeline structure.

(A) Latent r0 bug fixed in ConformalCI(). r0 was assigned only inside the
    `weighted == TRUE` branch but referenced in the return list. Initialised
    to NULL at the top of the function so the return is always well-defined.
    Real-data calls all set weighted = TRUE, so the bug never bit, but it
    was a foot-gun for anyone extending the code.

(B) Removed three vestigial `if (TRUE) { ... }` wrappers around the
    second-half (UC counterfactual) runs in each analysis block. These were
    leftovers from Patch 4 (which wrapped them in `if (FALSE)` to skip
    them) and Patch 6 (which flipped them to `if (TRUE)` to re-enable
    them). The published version unwraps them entirely.

(C) Clipping Option 2 implemented. The four methods produce intervals on
    a score scale that can extend below 0 or above 1, even though the
    outcome is binary. Previously, the plot data frames used clipped
    intervals (pmin(1, pmax(0, .))) and coverage / average length were
    computed from those clipped values. Now:
      - Each plotdat frame holds BOTH clipped columns (for plot display)
        and raw `*_raw` columns (unclipped).
      - cov_full_* (full-population coverage, computed from the raw columns)
        and the per-method average length (computed on the [0,1]-clipped
        columns) are now reported directly in each 2x2 panel TITLE as
        "CP ... , AL ...". The separate combined_summary / const_summary
        data.frames that previously printed these were removed (Request-3):
        CP and AL travel with each plot, so the standalone tables only
        duplicated that information.
      - A new `clipping-diagnostic` chunk reports, per method, how often
        clipping changed the interval and the pre/post difference in
        average length and coverage. Reviewers can see at a glance the
        size of the clipping effect.

(D) [BEHAVIOR-CHANGING — verify before publishing] Companion file
    multisource_fixed_patch7.Rmd had duplicate function definitions
    removed (see its own changelog). One of those removals — the simpler
    glmnet-only ASR/localASR/CQR chunk — was previously overwriting the
    binary-aware (SuperLearner-binomial) versions defined above. With
    the binary outcome dead_60 in {0,1}, the binary-aware path is the
    one that should run; after the cleanup, it does. If any previously
    reported figure was produced using the ridge-on-binary path, the
    Patch 7 numbers will differ. Re-run and compare before relying on
    Patch 7 outputs for publication.

mu_hat machinery is preserved everywhere (kept as a diagnostic, as
requested).

## Function Definitions

## Figure 2
### genY.R
```{r}
genY <- function(X){
  n <- nrow(X)
  2 / (1 + exp(-12 * (X[, 1] - 0.5))) * 2 / (1 + exp(-12 * (X[, 2] - 0.5))) + rnorm(n)
}

genY_singlestage <- function(X,T){
  n <- length(T)
  Y <- 1+X[,1]-X[,2]+X[,3]^{3}+exp(X[,4])+T*(3-5*X[,1]+2*X[,2]-3*X[,3]+X[,4])+(1+T)*(1+X[,1]+X[,2]+X[,3]+X[,4])*rnorm(n)
  return(Y)
}

genY_twostage <- function(X1,X2,T1,T2){
  n <- length(T1)
  Y <- 1+X1+T1*(1-3*(X1-0.2)^{2})+X2+T2*(1-5*(X2-0.4)^{2})+(1+0.5*T1-T1*X1+0.5*T2-T2*X2)*rnorm(n,0,sd=0.4)
  return(Y)
  }
```


### conformalCI_transferL_Yscore.R
```{r}
predict.conformalSplit2 <- function(Yhat_test,Yscore, wt,wt_test,
                                   alpha = 0.1,
                                   wthigh = 20, wtlow = 0.05,type,side){
    
    avg_wt <- mean(c(wt, wt_test))
    wt <- censoring(wt / avg_wt, wthigh, wtlow)
    wt_test <- censoring(wt_test / avg_wt, wthigh, wtlow)
   
    totw <- sum(wt)
    wt <- wt / totw
    qt <- (1 + wt_test / totw) * (1 - alpha)
    qt <- pmin(qt, 1)
    Yslack <- weightedConformalCutoff(Yscore, wt, qt)
    
    if (type == "CQR" && side == "two"){
        Ylo <- Yhat_test[, 1] - Yslack
        Yup <- Yhat_test[, 2] + Yslack
    } else if (type == "mean" && side == "two"){
        Ylo <- Yhat_test - Yslack
        Yup <- Yhat_test + Yslack
    } else if (side == "above"){
        Ylo <- -Inf
        Yup <- Yhat_test + Yslack
    } else if (side == "below"){
        Ylo <- Yhat_test - Yslack
        Yup <- Inf
    }
    
    res <- data.frame(lower = Ylo, upper = Yup)
    return(list(res=res,Yslack=Yslack))
}
######################################
#X,Y,T: X is a matrix, Y is a vector, T is a binary variable 0/1 (behavior policy)
#Deta: is the parameter vector for target policy
#Xtest: is the dataframe for test data
#method: "Sweight"(single weighted,split-and-sample in paper) B=1, "Dweight"(double weighted) B=1, "BootSweight" i.e. B=100, "BootDweight" i.e. B=100 
#B: resampling times for bootstrap
#trainprop: proportion of sample for training, including propensity score estimation and regression estimation
#psfun: propensity score estimation method("Boosting", "RF", "Logistic", "PenLogistic")
#psparams: parameters for psfun
#outfun: regression estimation method("quantRF", "quantBoosting", "quantBART")
#outparams: parameters for outfun
#quantiles: 0.05,0.95 quantile levels for regression prediction for "CQR"
#type: conformal quantile regression("CQR") and mean regression("mean")
#side: "two", "above" and "below" confidence interval with quantile regression 
#weighted: "TRUE"(estimated weights), "FALSE"(unweighted CQR) or user-specified weights vector for weighted conformal prediction
#alpha: confidence level
#wthigh/wtlow: upper and lower bounds for weights


ConformalCI <- function(X,Y,T,Deta,Xtest,method,B=1,trainprop,psfun,psparams,outfun,outparams,quantiles,type,side,weighted,alpha,wthigh,wtlow,wttl,wttl_test){
####added wttl as the weight for covariate shift   
  
  YBleft <- NULL
  YBright <- NULL
  Nts <- NULL
  ##### PATCH 3: track per-test-patient point estimates (Yhat_test) across
  ##### bootstrap iterations. For type='mean', Yhat_test IS the interval midpoint.
  mu_hat_accum <- NULL
  ##### END PATCH 3 init
  ##### CLEANUP: initialize r0 to NULL so the return list is well-defined
  ##### even when weighted!=TRUE (formerly, r0 was set inside the
  ##### `weighted==TRUE` branch only and could be undefined/stale).
  r0 <- NULL

  #random sample from binary varibale(A) B times
  for (b in 1:B) {
  n <- length(Y)
  #split samples for training and calibration
  YY <- Y
  YY[!T] <- NA
  T <- as.numeric(!is.na(YY))
  res <- SampleSplit(YY,trainprop)
  #res$trainid: index for all training
  #res$trainid1: index for all training with T=1
  #!!!need to select T=1 first and then select trainid1
  #res$trainid0: index for all training with T=0
  
  #estimate the propensity score
  Xtrain <- X[res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
  Ttrain <- T[res$trainid]
  PSFit_T <- PropScore(Ttrain,Xtrain,psfun, psparams)
  
  #estimate weights for testing data
  ps_T_test <- PSFit_T(Xtest)
  Xtest <- as.matrix(Xtest)
  ps_D_test <- exp(cbind(1,Xtest)%*%Deta)/(1+exp(cbind(1,Xtest)%*%Deta))
  ps_test <- ps_T_test*(1-ps_T_test)/(ps_T_test*(1-ps_D_test)+ps_D_test*(1-ps_T_test)) 
  
  
  #estimate the propensity score for binary A
  tp_T <- PSFit_T(X)
  tp_D <- exp(cbind(1,X)%*%Deta)/(1+exp(cbind(1,X)%*%Deta))
  tp_A <- tp_D*(1-tp_T)/(tp_D*(1-tp_T)+tp_T*(1-tp_D))
  

    A <- rbinom(n = n, size = 1, prob=tp_A)
    O <- I(T==A)
    Nts[b] <- sum(O)
    #quantile regression fitting after selecting A=T
    X1 <- X[res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
    Y1 <- Y[res$trainid]
    #select O=1 from training data
    ind <- which(O[res$trainid] == 1)
    Xtrain <- X1[ind, ,drop=FALSE]
    Ytrain <- Y1[ind]
    OutputFit <- QuantileReg(Ytrain,Xtrain,outfun,outparams,quantiles)
    Yhat_test <- OutputFit(Xtest)
    
    if(method == "Sweight" | method == "BootSweight"){
      #data for validation
      X0 <- X[-res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
      Y0 <- Y[-res$trainid]
      ind <- which(O[-res$trainid] == 1)
      Xval <- X0[ind, ,drop=FALSE]
      Yval <- Y0[ind]
      ps_T_val <- PSFit_T(as.data.frame(Xval))
      Yhat_val <- OutputFit(Xval)
      
      Xval <- as.matrix(Xval)
      ps_D_val <- exp(cbind(1,Xval)%*%Deta)/(1+exp(cbind(1,Xval)%*%Deta))
      ps_val <- ps_T_val*(1-ps_T_val)/(ps_T_val*(1-ps_D_val)+ps_D_val*(1-ps_T_val)) 
      
      ####subsample wttl, wttl is for both train and val
      wttl0 = wttl[-res$trainid]
      wttl_val = wttl0[ind]
      
    
      }else if(method == "Dweight" | method== "BootDweight"){
      #regression for validation
      Xval <- X[-res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
      Yval <- Y[-res$trainid]
      ps_T_val <- PSFit_T(as.data.frame(Xval))
      Yhat_val <- OutputFit(Xval)
      
      Xval <- as.matrix(Xval)
      ps_D_val <- exp(cbind(1,Xval)%*%Deta)/(1+exp(cbind(1,Xval)%*%Deta))
      ps_val <- ps_T_val*(1-ps_T_val)/(ps_T_val*(1-ps_D_val)+ps_D_val*(1-ps_T_val)) 
      ps_A_val <- ps_D_val*(1-ps_T_val)/(ps_D_val*(1-ps_T_val)+ps_T_val*(1-ps_D_val))
      ps_A_val[which(T[-res$trainid]==0)] <- 1-ps_A_val[which(T[-res$trainid]==0)]
      ps_val <- ps_val/ps_A_val
      
      #### wttl is for both train and val
      wttl_val= wttl[-res$trainid]
    }

    Yscore <- conformalScore(Yval, Yhat_val, type, side)

    #construct the confidence interval by weighted CP
    if(length(weighted)>1){
      wt <- weighted[1:n]
      if(method == "Sweight" | method == "BootSweight"){
        wt <- wt[-res$trainid]
        ind <- which(O[-res$trainid] == 1)
        wt <- wt[ind]
      }else if(method == "Dweight" | method == "BootDweight"){
        wt <- wt[-res$trainid]
        }
      wt_test <- weighted[-(1:n)]
      PredInt<- predict.conformalSplit(Yhat_test, Yscore,wt,wt_test,alpha,wthigh,wtlow,type,side)
    }else if(weighted==TRUE){
      ####wt <- 1/ps_val
      ####add wttl, wttl_test
      wt <- (1/ps_val)*wttl_val
      wt_test <- (1/ps_test)*wttl_test
      ####PredInt<- predict.conformalSplit(Yhat_test, Yscore,wt,wt_test,alpha,wthigh,wtlow,type,side)
      PredInt<- predict.conformalSplit2(Yhat_test, Yscore,wt,wt_test,alpha,wthigh,wtlow,type,side)
      r0=PredInt$Yslack
      print(r0)
      PredInt=PredInt$res
    }else if(weighted==FALSE){
      wt <- rep(1,length(ps_val))
      wt_test <- rep(1,length(ps_test))
      PredInt<- predict.conformalSplit(Yhat_test, Yscore,wt,wt_test,alpha,wthigh,wtlow,type,side)
    }
    
    YBleft <- rbind(YBleft,PredInt[,1])
    YBright <- rbind(YBright,PredInt[,2])
      ##### PATCH 3: accumulate point estimates (Yhat_test) across bootstrap iterations
      mu_hat_accum <- rbind(mu_hat_accum, as.numeric(Yhat_test))
      ##### END PATCH 3 rbind
  } 
  
  #if bootstrap used, combine multiple CI to a single one
  #otherwise, a single CI is produced
  lefts <- NULL
  rights <- NULL
  Lens <- NULL
  if((B>1) & (method == "BootSweight" | method == "BootDweight")){
    
    ntest <- nrow(Xtest)
    for (j in 1:ntest) {
      
      Ys <- c(YBleft[,j],YBright[,j])
      Ws <- c(rep(1,nrow(YBleft)),rep(1,nrow(YBright)))
      Ss <- c(rep(1,nrow(YBleft)),rep(0,nrow(YBright)))
      #tol <- B*(1-gamma)
      tol <- B/2
      
      ind <- order(Ys)
      Ys <- Ys[ind]
      Ws <- Ws[ind]
      Ss <- Ss[ind]
      count <- 0
      leftpoints <- NULL
      rightpoints <- NULL
      
      for (i in 1:length(Ys)) {
        if(Ss[i]==1){
          count <- count+Ws[i]
          if((count>tol)&(count-Ws[i]<=tol)){
            leftpoints <- c(leftpoints,Ys[i])
          }
        }else if(Ss[i]==0){
          if((count>tol)&(count-Ws[i]<=tol)){
            rightpoints <- c(rightpoints,Ys[i])
          }
          count <- count-Ws[i]
        }
      }
      lefts[[j]] <- leftpoints
      rights[[j]] <- rightpoints
      Lens[j] <- sum(rightpoints-leftpoints)
    }
  }else if((B==1) & (method == "Sweight" | method == "Dweight")){
    for (j in 1:ntest) {
    lefts[[j]] <- YBleft[j]
    rights[[j]] <- YBright[j]
    Lens[j] <- YBright[j]-YBleft[j]
    }
  }
  
  ##### PATCH 3: collapse bootstrap-stacked predictions to per-patient point estimate
  if (!is.null(mu_hat_accum)) {
    mu_hat <- colMeans(mu_hat_accum, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    mu_hat <- NULL
  }
  ##### END PATCH 3 mu_hat
  ##### PATCH 3: include mu_hat in the returned list
  return(list(lefts=lefts, rights=rights, Lens=Lens, Nts=Nts, r0=r0, mu_hat=mu_hat))
}
```

### Calculating wttl for test and val
```{r}
######################################
#X,Y,T: X is a matrix, Y is a vector, T is a binary variable 0/1 (behavior policy)
#Deta: is the parameter vector for target policy
#Xtest: is the dataframe for test data
#method: "Sweight"(single weighted,split-and-sample in paper) B=1, "Dweight"(double weighted) B=1, "BootSweight" i.e. B=100, "BootDweight" i.e. B=100 
#B: resampling times for bootstrap
#trainprop: proportion of sample for training, including propensity score estimation and regression estimation
#psfun: propensity score estimation method("Boosting", "RF", "Logistic", "PenLogistic")
#psparams: parameters for psfun
#outfun: regression estimation method("quantRF", "quantBoosting", "quantBART")
#outparams: parameters for outfun
#quantiles: 0.05,0.95 quantile levels for regression prediction for "CQR"
#type: conformal quantile regression("CQR") and mean regression("mean")
#side: "two", "above" and "below" confidence interval with quantile regression 
#weighted: "TRUE"(estimated weights), "FALSE"(unweighted CQR) or user-specified weights vector for weighted conformal prediction
#alpha: confidence level
#wthigh/wtlow: upper and lower bounds for weights

#library(CVXR)
delta.tilde.prob <- function(x, alphas) {
  # x: covariate vecter or matrix including intercep 1
  # return: the probability of \widetilde{\delta}=1 given x
  x.alpha <- x %*% alphas
  prob <- exp(x.alpha)/(1 + exp(x.alpha))
  return(prob)
}

####### the functions used for the proposed transfer learner method #######
cost2 <- function(alphas, x.in.rct, x.in.rwe, N) {
  # the cost function of the first parametric weighting method
  part1 <- sum(x.in.rct %*% as.matrix(alphas, length(alphas), 1))
  part2 <- mean(log(1 + exp(x.in.rwe %*% as.matrix(alphas, length(alphas), 1))))*N
  return(part2-part1)
} 
cost <- function(alphas, x.in.rct, left.hand, N) {
  # the cost function of the second parametric weighting method
  right.hand <- apply(x.in.rct / c(delta.tilde.prob(x.in.rct, alphas)), 2, sum)/N
  diff <- right.hand - left.hand
  return(sqrt(mean(diff**2)))
}
entr_balance <- function(tol, x.in.rct, x.in.rwe) {
  # the optimization problem for the nonparametric weighting method
  n <- dim(x.in.rct)[1] 
  w <- Variable(n)
  p <- dim(x.in.rct)[2]-1
  # entr: is the element-wise entropy atom
  objective <- Maximize(sum(entr(w))) 
  constraints <- list(w >= 0, sum(w) == 1)
  for (k in 1:p) {
    constraints <- c(constraints, abs(sum(w*x.in.rct[,k+1]) - mean(x.in.rwe[,k+1])) <= tol*sd(x.in.rwe[,k+1]))
    constraints <- c(constraints, abs(sum(w*(x.in.rct[,k+1]**2)) - mean(x.in.rwe[,k+1]**2)) <= tol*sd(x.in.rwe[,k+1]**2)) ## added for the misspecify
  }
  prob <- Problem(objective, constraints)
  w.tilde <- rep(0, n)
  tryCatch(
    expr = {
      result <- suppressWarnings(solve(prob))  
      w.tilde <- result$getValue(w)
      if (is.na(w.tilde)[1]) {
        w.tilde <- rep(0,n)
      }
    },
    error = function(e) {
      # print("error")
    }
  )
  return(w.tilde)
}
weight_tuned_entr <- function(tols, x.in.rct, x.in.rwe, prop=0.5, smps=10) {
  # Evaluate covariate balance with bootstrap samples to choose tuning parameters: 
  #   the degree of approximate balance sigma_k
  n <- dim(x.in.rct)[1]
  sds <- apply(x.in.rwe, 2, sd)
  means <- apply(x.in.rwe, 2, mean)
  sds2 <- apply(x.in.rwe**2, 2, sd)
  moment2 <- apply(x.in.rwe**2, 2, mean)
  cov.diff.bars <- c()
  w.tildes <- matrix(NA, n, length(tols))
  for (i in 1:length(tols)) {
    tol <- tols[i]
    w.tilde <- entr_balance(tol, x.in.rct, x.in.rwe)
    w.tilde[w.tilde < 0] <- 0 ## the optimization results sometimes return negative weights, so clip them to 0
    if (sum(w.tilde)==0) {
      cov.diff.bar <- 1e+10
    } else {
      w.tildes[,i] <- w.tilde
      cov.diffs <- c()
      for (s in 1:smps) {
        boot.ind <- sample.int(n, round(prop*n), replace=TRUE)
        x.in.rct.boot <- x.in.rct[boot.ind,]
        w.tilde.boot <- w.tilde[boot.ind]
        cov.diff <- (apply(x.in.rct.boot*w.tilde.boot, 2, sum)/sum(w.tilde.boot) -  means)[-1] / sds[-1] ## remember check this again, should also add 2nd moment diff?
        cov.diff.moment2 <- (apply(x.in.rct.boot**2*w.tilde.boot, 2, sum)/sum(w.tilde.boot) -  moment2)[-1] / sds2[-1]
        cov.diffs <- c(cov.diffs, sum((c(cov.diff, cov.diff.moment2))**2)) ## L2 measure
      }
      cov.diff.bar <- mean(cov.diffs)
    }
    cov.diff.bars <- c(cov.diff.bars, cov.diff.bar)
  }
  tuned.tol <- tols[which.min(cov.diff.bars)]
  if (min(cov.diff.bars) < 1e+10) {
    return(w.tildes[, which.min(cov.diff.bars)])
  } else {
    stop('************ optimization not feasible *****************')
  }
}

learn_weights <- function(x.in.rct, x.in.rwe, w.method,  N) {
  # w.method: 1, 2, 3, 4
  n <- dim(x.in.rct)[1]
  p <- dim(x.in.rct)[2] - 1
  if (w.method == 1) {
    # unweighted
    w.tilde <- rep(1, n)
    w.tilde.rwe <- rep(1, dim(x.in.rwe)[1])
  } else if (w.method == 2) {
    # the first parametric weighting method
    
      opt2 <- optim(rep(0,p+1), cost2, x.in.rct=x.in.rct, x.in.rwe=x.in.rwe, N=N, method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(maxit=10000))
      (alphas.hat2 <- opt2$par)
      w.tilde <- 1 + 1/(exp(x.in.rct %*% as.matrix(alphas.hat2, length(alphas.hat2), 1)))
      w.tilde.rwe <- 1 + 1/(exp(x.in.rwe %*% as.matrix(alphas.hat2, length(alphas.hat2), 1)))
    
  } else if (w.method == 3) {
    # the second parametric weighting method
    left.hand <- apply(x.in.rwe, 2, mean)
    
      opt <- optim(rep(0, p+1), cost, x.in.rct=x.in.rct, left.hand=left.hand, N=N, method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(maxit=10000))
      (alphas.hat3 <- opt$par)
      w.tilde <- 1 + 1/(exp(x.in.rct %*% as.matrix(alphas.hat3, length(alphas.hat3), 1)))
      w.tilde.rwe <- 1 + 1/(exp(x.in.rwe %*% as.matrix(alphas.hat3, length(alphas.hat3), 1)))
    
  } else if (w.method == 4) {
    # nonparametric weighting
    w.tilde <- weight_tuned_entr(tols=c(0.000, 0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.010, 0.020, 0.050, 0.100, 0.200, 0.500, 1.000),
                                 x.in.rct, x.in.rwe)
  } else if (w.method == 5) {
    # the first parametric weighting method with true alphas
    
      #opt2 <- optim(rep(0,p+1), cost2, x.in.rct=x.in.rct, x.in.rwe=x.in.rwe, N=N, method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(maxit=10000))
      #(alphas.hat2 <- opt2$par)
    (alphas.hat2 <- c(alphas.true))
      w.tilde <- 1 + 1/(exp(x.in.rct %*% as.matrix(alphas.hat2, length(alphas.hat2), 1)))
      w.tilde.rwe <- 1 + 1/(exp(x.in.rwe %*% as.matrix(alphas.hat2, length(alphas.hat2), 1)))
    
  } else {
    stop("Wrong input for weighting method")
  }
  ####w.tilde
  return(list(w.tilde.rct=w.tilde, w.tilde.rwe=w.tilde.rwe))
}
```

```{r}
## weightedConformalCutoff <- function(score, weight, qt){

find_inds <- function(a, b){
    n <- length(a)
    b <- b - 1e-12
    ## n + 1 - rank(-c(a, b), ties.method = "first")[-(1:n)] + rank(-b, ties.method = "first")
    rank(c(a, b), ties.method = "first")[-(1:n)] - rank(b, ties.method = "first") + 1
}

## weightedConformalCutoff0 <- function(score, weight, qt){

##     })

## }

weightedConformalCutoff <- function(score, weight, qt){
    ord <- order(score)
    weight <- weight[ord]
    score <- score[ord]
    cw <- cumsum(weight)
    inds <- find_inds(cw, qt)    
    cutoff <- score[inds]
    return(cutoff)
}

conformalScore <- function(Y, Yhat, type, side){
    if (is.vector(Y) || (is.matrix(Y) && ncol(Y) == 1)){
        if (type == "CQR" && side == "two"){
            score <- pmax(Yhat[, 1] - Y, Y - Yhat[, 2])
        } else if (type == "mean" && side == "two"){
            score <- abs(Yhat - Y)
        } else if (side == "above"){
            score <- Y - Yhat
        } else if (side == "below"){
            score <- Yhat - Y
        }
    } else if (is.matrix(Y) && ncol(Y) == 2){
        score <- pmax(Yhat[, 1] - Y[, 1], Y[, 2] - Yhat[, 2])
    }
    return(score)
}

conformalScoreClass <- function(Y, phat, type, wt){
    ncl <- nlevels(Y)
    if (type == "weighted"){
        phat <- row_quo(phat, wt)
    }
    Yid <- as.numeric(Y)
    score <- phat[cbind(1:length(Y), Yid)]
    return(score)
}


## Truncate a sequence from both sides
censoring <- function(x, high = 20, low = 0.05){
    pmin(pmax(x, low), high)
}


predict.conformalSplit <- function(Yhat_test,Yscore, wt,wt_test,
                                   alpha = 0.1,
                                   wthigh = 20, wtlow = 0.05,type,side){
    
    avg_wt <- mean(c(wt, wt_test))
    wt <- censoring(wt / avg_wt, wthigh, wtlow)
    wt_test <- censoring(wt_test / avg_wt, wthigh, wtlow)
   
    totw <- sum(wt)
    wt <- wt / totw
    qt <- (1 + wt_test / totw) * (1 - alpha)
    qt <- pmin(qt, 1)
    Yslack <- weightedConformalCutoff(Yscore, wt, qt)
    
    if (type == "CQR" && side == "two"){
        Ylo <- Yhat_test[, 1] - Yslack
        Yup <- Yhat_test[, 2] + Yslack
    } else if (type == "mean" && side == "two"){
        Ylo <- Yhat_test - Yslack
        Yup <- Yhat_test + Yslack
    } else if (side == "above"){
        Ylo <- -Inf
        Yup <- Yhat_test + Yslack
    } else if (side == "below"){
        Ylo <- Yhat_test - Yslack
        Yup <- Inf
    }
    
    res <- data.frame(lower = Ylo, upper = Yup)
    return(res)
}
```

```{r}
## Guess the type of a variable
guessClass <- function(x){
    if (length(unique(x)) == 2 || is.logical(x) || (is.factor(x) && nlevels(x) == 2)){
        dist <- "bernoulli"
    } else if (is.factor(x) && nlevels(x) > 2){
        dist <- "multinomial"
    } else if (is.numeric(x)){
        dist <- "gaussian"
    }
    return(dist)
}

## quantile random forest. grf package needed
quantRF <- function(Y, X, Xtest, quantiles, ...){
    fit <- grf::quantile_forest(X, Y, quantiles = quantiles, ...)
    res <- predict(fit, Xtest, quantiles = quantiles)
    res <- res[[1]]
    if (length(quantiles) == 1){
        res <- as.numeric(res)
    } else {
        res <- as.matrix(res)
    }
    return(res)
}

## random forest. randomForest package needed
RF <- function(Y, X, Xtest, ...){
    dist <- guessClass(Y)
    if (dist == "gaussian"){
        fit <- randomForest::randomForest(x = X, y = Y, ...)
        res <- predict(fit, newdata = Xtest)
        res <- as.numeric(res)
    } else if (dist == "bernoulli"){
        if (!is.factor(Y)){
            Y <- as.factor(Y)
        }
        fit <- randomForest::randomForest(x = X, y = Y, ...)
        res <- predict(fit, newdata = Xtest, type = "prob")
        res <- as.numeric(res[, 2])
    } else if (dist == "multinomial"){
        if (!is.factor(Y)){
            Y <- as.factor(Y)
        }
        fit <- randomForest::randomForest(x = X, y = Y, ...)
        res <- predict(fit, newdata = Xtest, type = "prob")
        res <- as.matrix(res)
    }
    return(res)
}

## quantile gradient boosting. gbm package needed
quantBoosting <- function(Y, X, Xtest, quantiles, n.trees = 100, ...){
    # if (class(X) != "data.frame"){
    #     X <- as.data.frame(X)
    #     Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    #     names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    # }
        X <- as.data.frame(X)
        Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
        names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    data <- data.frame(Y = Y, X)
    fit <- gbm::gbm(Y ~ ., distribution = list(name = "quantile", alpha = quantiles[1]), data = data, n.trees = n.trees, ...)
    res <- predict(fit, Xtest, type = "response", n.trees = n.trees)
    if (length(quantiles) == 2){
        fit2 <- gbm::gbm(Y ~ ., distribution = list(name = "quantile", alpha = quantiles[2]), data = data, n.trees = n.trees, ...)
        res2 <- predict(fit2, Xtest, type = "response", n.trees = n.trees)
        res <- cbind(res, res2)
    }
    return(res)
}

## gradient boosting. gbm package needed
Boosting <- function(Y, X, Xtest, n.trees = 100, ...){
    # if (class(X) != "data.frame"){
    #     X <- as.data.frame(X)
    #     Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    #     names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    # }
    X <- as.data.frame(X)
    Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    distribution <- guessClass(Y)
    if (distribution == "bernoulli" && is.factor(Y)){
        Y <- as.numeric(Y) - 1
    }
    data <- data.frame(Y = Y, X)
    fit <- gbm::gbm(Y ~ ., distribution = distribution, data = data, n.trees = n.trees, ...)
    res <- predict(fit, Xtest, type = "response", n.trees = n.trees)
    if (distribution == "multinomial"){
        res <- matrix(res, nrow = nrow(Xtest))
    }
    return(res)
}

## Logistic
Logistic <- function(Y, X, Xtest, ...){
    # if (class(X) != "data.frame"){
    #     X <- as.data.frame(X)
    #     Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    #     names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    # }
    X <- as.data.frame(X)
    Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    distribution <- guessClass(Y)
    if (distribution == "bernoulli" && is.factor(Y)){
        Y <- as.numeric(Y) - 1
    }
    data <- data.frame(Y = Y, X)
    fit <- stats::glm(Y ~ ., family=binomial(link='logit'),data=data)
    res <- predict(fit, Xtest, type = "response")
    if (distribution == "multinomial"){
        res <- matrix(res, nrow = nrow(Xtest))
    }
    return(res)
}


## PenLogistic
PenLogistic <- function(Y, X, Xtest, ...){
    # if (class(X) != "data.frame"){
    #     X <- as.data.frame(X)
    #     Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    #     names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    # }
    X <- as.matrix(X)
    Xtest <- as.matrix(Xtest)
    names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    distribution <- guessClass(Y)
    if (distribution == "bernoulli" && is.factor(Y)){
        Y <- as.numeric(Y) - 1
    }
    data <- data.frame(Y = Y, X)
    fit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(X, Y, family="binomial",alpha = 1)
    res <- predict(fit, newx=Xtest, type = "response",s="lambda.min")
    if (distribution == "multinomial"){
        res <- matrix(res, nrow = nrow(Xtest))
    }
    return(res)
}


## posterior quantiles of BART. bartMachine package needed
quantBART <- function(Y, X, Xtest, quantiles,
                      ndpost = 100, ...){
    # if (class(X) != "data.frame"){
    #     X <- as.data.frame(X)
    #     Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    #     names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    # }
    X <- as.data.frame(X)
    Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    fit <- bartMachine::bartMachine(X, Y, verbose = FALSE)
    if (length(quantiles) == 2){
        if (sum(quantiles) != 1){
            warning("Two quantiles should sum up to 1.")
        }
        ci_conf <- quantiles[2] - quantiles[1]
        res <- bartMachine::calc_prediction_intervals(
                                fit, new_data = Xtest,
                                pi_conf = 0.95)$interval
        res <- as.matrix(res)
    } else if (length(quantiles) == 1){
        if (quantiles[1] > 0.5){
            ci_conf <- 2 * quantiles[1]
            res <- bartMachine::calc_prediction_intervals(
                                    fit, new_data = Xtest,
                                    pi_conf = 0.95)$interval[, 2]
            res <- as.numeric(res)
        }  else{
            ci_conf <- 2 * (1 - quantiles[1])
            res <- bartMachine::calc_prediction_intervals(
                                    fit, new_data = Xtest,
                                    pi_conf = 0.95)$interval[, 1]
            res <- as.numeric(res)
        }
    }
    return(res)
}

## BART. bartMachine package needed
BART <- function(Y, X, Xtest,
                 ndpost = 100, ...){
    # if (class(X) != "data.frame"){
    #     X <- as.data.frame(X)
    #     Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    #     names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    # }
    X <- as.data.frame(X)
    Xtest <- as.data.frame(Xtest)
    names(Xtest) <- names(X)
    fit <- bartMachine::bartMachine(X, Y, verbose = FALSE)
    res <- predict(fit, Xtest)
    return(res)
}
```

```{r}
## Convert a valid psfun string to the function
str_psfun <- function(method){
  if (method == "RF"){
    if (!requireNamespace("randomForest")){
      stop("randomForest package needs to be installed")
    }
    return(RF)
  } else if (method == "Boosting"){
    if (!requireNamespace("gbm")){
      stop("gbm package needs to be installed")
    }
    return(Boosting)
  } else {
    stop(paste0(method, " is not supported. Please input a valid string or a function that meets the minimal requirements described in the man page"))
  }
}


#psfun: only Boosting and RF are supported
PropScore <- function(Ttrain,Xtrain,psfun, psparams){
  
  if (is.null(psfun)){
    psfun <- Boosting
  } else if (is.character(psfun)){
    psfun <- str_psfun(psfun[1])
  } 
  
  psparams0 <- psparams
  psparams <- c(list(Y = Ttrain, X = Xtrain), psparams0)
  PropScorefun <- function(X){
    ps <- do.call(psfun, c(list(Xtest = X), psparams))
    ps
  }
  PropScorefun
}
```

```{r}
QuantileReg <- function(Ytrain,Xtrain,outfun,outparams=NULL,quantiles){
  outparams <- c(outparams, list(quantiles = quantiles))
  outparams <- c(list(Y = Ytrain, X = Xtrain), outparams)
  
  Ymodel <- function(X){
    fit <- do.call(outfun, c(outparams, list(Xtest = X)))
    fit
  }
  Ymodel
}
```

### samplesplit.R
```{r}
############################################
#split samples to training and validation
#for both T=1 and T=0
SampleSplit <- function(Y,trainprop){
  T <- as.numeric(!is.na(Y))
  inds1 <- which(T == 1)
  inds0 <- which(T == 0)
  n1 <- length(inds1)
  n0 <- length(inds0)
  trainid1 <- sample(n1, floor(n1 * trainprop))
  trainid0 <- sample(n0, floor(n0 * trainprop))
  trainid <- c(inds1[trainid1], inds0[trainid0])
  return(list(trainid=trainid, trainid1=trainid1,trainid0=trainid0))
}
```

### naive.R
```{r}
######################################
###### 2022.4.13 zhang yingying ######

#X,Y,T: X is a matrix, Y is a vector, T is a binary variable 0/1 (behavior policy)
#Deta: is the parameter vector for target policy
#Xtest: is the dataframe for test data

#naive method: select D=T
#trainprop: proportion of sample for training, including propensity score estimation and regression estimation
#psfun: propensity score estimation method("Boosting", "RF", "Logistic", "PenLogistic")
#psparams: parameters for psfun
#outfun: regression estimation method("quantRF", "quantBoosting", "quantBART")
#outparams: parameters for outfun
#quantiles: 0.05,0.95 quantile levels for regression prediction for "CQR"
#type: conformal quantile regression("CQR") and mean regression("mean")
#side: "two", "above" and "below" confidence interval with quantile regression 
#alpha: confidence level
#wthigh/wtlow: upper and lower bounds for weights


Naive <- function(X,Y,T,Deta,Xtest,trainprop,psfun,psparams,outfun,outparams,quantiles,type,side,alpha,wthigh,wtlow){
  
  n <- length(Y)
  #split samples for training and calibration
  YY <- Y
  YY[!T] <- NA
  T <- as.numeric(!is.na(YY))
  res <- SampleSplit(YY,trainprop)
  #res$trainid: index for all training
  #res$trainid1: index for all training with T=1
  #!!!need to select T=1 first and then select trainid1
  #res$trainid0: index for all training with T=0
  
  #estimate the propensity score
  Xtrain <- X[res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
  Ttrain <- T[res$trainid]
  PSFit_T <- PropScore(Ttrain,Xtrain,psfun, psparams)
  
  #estimate the propensity score for binary A
  tp_T <- PSFit_T(X)
  tp_D <- exp(cbind(1,X)%*%Deta)/(1+exp(cbind(1,X)%*%Deta))
  ps_T_test <- PSFit_T(Xtest)
  
  #random sample from binary varibale(D)
  D <- rbinom(n = n, size = 1, prob=tp_D)
  O <- I(T==D)
  Nts <- sum(O)
  #quantile regression fitting after selecting A=T
  X1 <- X[res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
  Y1 <- Y[res$trainid]
  #select O=1 from training data
  ind <- which(O[res$trainid] == 1)
  Xtrain <- X1[ind, ,drop=FALSE]
  Ytrain <- Y1[ind]
  OutputFit <- QuantileReg(Ytrain,Xtrain,outfun,outparams,quantiles)
  Yhat_test <- OutputFit(Xtest)
    
  #data for validation
  X0 <- X[-res$trainid, ,drop=FALSE]
  Y0 <- Y[-res$trainid]
  ind <- which(O[-res$trainid] == 1)
  Xval <- X0[ind, ,drop=FALSE]
  Yval <- Y0[ind]
  ps_T_val <- PSFit_T(as.data.frame(Xval))
  Yhat_val <- OutputFit(Xval)
      
  Yscore <- conformalScore(Yval, Yhat_val, type, side)
  #construct the confidence interval by weighted CP
  wt <- rep(1,length(ps_T_val))
  wt_test <- rep(1,length(ps_T_test))
  PredInt<- predict.conformalSplit(Yhat_test, Yscore,wt,wt_test,alpha,wthigh,wtlow,type,side)
 
  lefts <- PredInt[,1]
  rights <- PredInt[,2]
  Lens <- rights-lefts
  
  return(list(lefts=lefts, rights=rights, Lens=Lens, Nts=Nts))
}

```

```{r}
genY_singlestage_ex <- function(X,T,site_num){
  n <- length(T)
  Y <- 1+X[,1]-X[,2]+site_num*X[,3]^{3}+exp(X[,4])+T*(3-5*X[,1]+2*X[,2]-3*X[,3]+X[,4])+(1+T)*(1+X[,1]+X[,2]+X[,3]+X[,4])*rnorm(n)
  return(Y)
}
```

## PATCH 9 — Smooth severity-adaptive (SOFA-graded) evaluation policy

The primary evaluation policy is now a SMOOTH, monotone function of SOFA
severity rather than a hard `sofa_total >= 4` threshold. Treating SOFA as a
ranked continuous severity index, the EGDT probability increases smoothly
with severity:
$$\pi_e(\text{EGDT}\mid X) = \mathrm{expit}\{\beta\,(\text{SOFA}-m)/s\},$$
where $m,s$ are the SOFA mean and SD on the target (UPMC) population and
$\beta>0$ controls steepness. This is a stochastic individualized treatment
rule: sicker patients are assigned a higher EGDT probability, with no
arbitrary cutpoint. The hard threshold is the limiting case $\beta\to\infty$.

Implementation: unlike the hard policy (which spliced two constant-policy
runs), a smooth policy is evaluated in a SINGLE run per block using the
method's own subsampling + weighting machinery. Choosing a MODERATE $\beta$
keeps $\pi_e$ away from 0/1, so the policy-shift subsampling retains enough
calibration units and avoids the variance inflation seen with the earlier
near-step 0.1/0.9 policy.

```{r patch6-define-policy}
##### PATCH 9: smooth severity-adaptive SOFA policy is now the primary.
##### pi_e(EGDT | X) = expit( beta * (sofa_total - m) / s ),  beta > 0.
#####
##### Code convention (see ConformalCI): tp_D = expit(Deta'[1,X]) is the
##### modeled probability of the CONTROL (UC) arm, so the EGDT evaluation
##### policy is pi_e(EGDT|X) = 1 - tp_D = expit(-Deta'[1,X]). Hence to obtain
##### pi_e(EGDT|X) = expit( beta*(sofa-m)/s ) we set
#####     Deta[intercept]   =  beta * m / s
#####     Deta[sofa column] = -beta / s
##### with all other Deta entries = 0.

sofa_col_idx <- which(colnames(Xtest) == "sofa_total")
stopifnot(length(sofa_col_idx) == 1)   # SOFA must be present exactly once

##### --- Tunable steepness of the severity-adaptive policy -------------------
##### beta_sofa = change in EGDT log-odds per 1 SD of SOFA.
#####   beta = 1.0 -> moderate grading (default): pi_e ~ 0.5 at mean SOFA,
#####                 ~0.27/0.73 at +-1 SD, ~0.12/0.88 at +-2 SD.
#####   larger beta  -> steeper, approaching the old hard >= 4 threshold.
#####   smaller beta -> flatter, approaching the constant 0.5 policy.
beta_sofa <- 1.0
##### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### Standardization constants: SOFA mean / SD on the TARGET (UPMC) population
##### where the policy is deployed. Held fixed so pi_e is a well-defined, known
##### function of X applied consistently to source and target data.
sofa_vec  <- as.numeric(Xtest[, "sofa_total"])
sofa_mean <- mean(sofa_vec)
sofa_sd   <- sd(sofa_vec)

Deta_smooth <- rep(0, ncol(Xtest) + 1)
Deta_smooth[1]                <-  beta_sofa * sofa_mean / sofa_sd   # intercept
Deta_smooth[1 + sofa_col_idx] <- -beta_sofa / sofa_sd              # SOFA slope

##### Constant all-EGDT policy retained for the constant-policy scenario / figure.
Deta_egdt <- c(-6, rep(0, ncol(Xtest)))   # all EGDT (tp_D ~ 0, pi_e(EGDT) ~ 1)
##### All-UC retained only for optional sensitivity (see the sensitivity stub).
Deta_uc   <- c( 6, rep(0, ncol(Xtest)))   # all UC   (tp_D ~ 1, pi_e(EGDT) ~ 0)

##### Per-patient EGDT policy value on the target population (diagnostics + the
##### figure's severity-gradient stripe).
pi_e_egdt_test <- as.numeric(1 / (1 + exp(cbind(1, as.matrix(Xtest)) %*% Deta_smooth)))
##### (legacy) high-severity indicator; kept only as an optional visual marker,
##### it no longer drives any splicing.
sofa_high_idx  <- sofa_vec >= 4

cat("\n=== PATCH 9 sanity check: smooth severity-adaptive EGDT policy ===\n")
cat("beta_sofa =", beta_sofa, "| SOFA mean =", round(sofa_mean, 2),
    "| SOFA sd =", round(sofa_sd, 2), "\n")
cat("UPMC sofa_total summary:\n"); print(summary(sofa_vec))
cat("Resulting pi_e(EGDT|X) summary:\n"); print(round(summary(pi_e_egdt_test), 3))
cat("pi_e(EGDT|X) quantiles (5/25/50/75/95%):\n")
print(round(quantile(pi_e_egdt_test, c(.05, .25, .5, .75, .95)), 3))
cat("=== End sanity check ===\n\n")
```

## Plot helper (defines make_panel for the figure chunks below)
```{r plot-helper}
library(ggplot2)
##### Helper: build a ranked-interval ggplot for one method.
##### PATCH 3: introduced black dot at interval midpoint as displayed point estimate.
##### PATCH 3 HOTFIX (Option C): switched from mu_hat to (lwr+upr)/2 for visual coherence.
##### PATCH 5: optional sofa_high_col argument adds a colored stripe under x-axis.
##### PATCH 6: REMOVED the displayed black dot. mu_hat is still computed and returned
##### in upmcIntv as a diagnostic. The interval midpoint is still computed internally
##### (df$.mid) because we use it for within-panel ranking, but it is no longer drawn
##### on the plot. The mu_col argument is kept for backward compatibility but is unused.
make_panel <- function(df, lwr_col, upr_col, mu_col, method_label, panel_color,
                       sofa_high_col = NULL, cov_full = NULL, sofa_val_col = NULL,
                       lwr_raw_col = NULL, upr_raw_col = NULL, al_full = NULL) {
  ##### Request-3: al_full (optional) is the method's average interval length on
  ##### the FULL target sample (computed by the caller on the [0,1]-clipped
  ##### intervals, matching the AL convention used elsewhere). When supplied it
  ##### is printed in the panel title next to coverage, so both CP and AL travel
  ##### with each plot and no separate summary table is needed.
  df$id <- seq_len(nrow(df))
  # Sort patients by interval midpoint (left to right: low predicted risk to high)
  ord <- order((df[[lwr_col]] + df[[upr_col]]) / 2)
  df <- df[ord, ]
  df$id <- seq_len(nrow(df))
  df$.mid <- (df[[lwr_col]] + df[[upr_col]]) / 2  # used for ranking only; not plotted
  ##### Request-2: an interval is colored ONLY when it covers THIS patient's
  ##### actual observed outcome upmc.dead_60 (the correct value, 0 = survived or
  ##### 1 = died) -- i.e. correct coverage of the true 0/1 label. It is faded
  ##### gray otherwise. The color is NOT keyed to whether the interval merely
  ##### touches 0 or 1 in the abstract, but to whether it covers the RIGHT one
  ##### for that patient, so the colored/gray split is exactly the coverage
  ##### event. Coverage for coloring uses the RAW interval columns when supplied,
  ##### so the colors match the reported coverage number (also computed on raw
  ##### intervals). This is a display encoding only: every displayed patient is
  ##### still shown, nothing is filtered, and the panel title still reports the
  ##### full-sample coverage.
  .lc <- if (!is.null(lwr_raw_col) && lwr_raw_col %in% names(df)) lwr_raw_col else lwr_col
  .uc <- if (!is.null(upr_raw_col) && upr_raw_col %in% names(df)) upr_raw_col else upr_col
  df$.covered <- (df[[.lc]] <= df$upmc.dead_60) & (df[[.uc]] >= df$upmc.dead_60)
  df$.covered[is.na(df$.covered)] <- FALSE
  df$.cov_grp <- ifelse(df$.covered, "covered", "missed")
  ##### PATCH 6 fix: if cov_full is supplied, use it for the title so the panel
  ##### title matches the full-population coverage that gets reported in tables.
  ##### Otherwise fall back to subsample coverage (computed on df), which is
  ##### what was shown previously but can disagree with the table by ~1-2 pp.
  if (is.null(cov_full)) {
    cov_for_title <- mean(df[[lwr_col]] <= df$upmc.dead_60 & df[[upr_col]] >= df$upmc.dead_60, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    cov_for_title <- cov_full
  }

  ##### PATCH 9: SOFA severity stripe under the x-axis.
  ##### If sofa_val_col is supplied -> CONTINUOUS gradient (light gray = low
  ##### SOFA, dark red = high SOFA), visualizing the ranked severity-adaptive
  ##### policy. Otherwise fall back to the legacy binary stripe (sofa_high_col).
  stripe_layer <- NULL
  if (!is.null(sofa_val_col) && sofa_val_col %in% names(df)) {
    sv  <- as.numeric(df[[sofa_val_col]])
    rng <- range(sv, na.rm = TRUE)
    sv01 <- (sv - rng[1]) / max(1e-8, diff(rng))
    sv01[is.na(sv01)] <- 0
    pal  <- grDevices::colorRamp(c("gray85", "firebrick"))
    cols <- grDevices::rgb(pal(sv01), maxColorValue = 255)
    stripe_df <- data.frame(xmin = df$id - 0.5, xmax = df$id + 0.5,
                            ymin = -0.07, ymax = -0.03)
    stripe_layer <- geom_rect(data = stripe_df,
                              aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                              fill = cols, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  } else if (!is.null(sofa_high_col) && sofa_high_col %in% names(df)) {
    stripe_df <- data.frame(
      xmin = df$id - 0.5, xmax = df$id + 0.5, ymin = -0.07, ymax = -0.03,
      sofa_high = as.logical(df[[sofa_high_col]])
    )
    stripe_df$fill <- ifelse(stripe_df$sofa_high, "firebrick", "gray70")
    stripe_layer <- geom_rect(data = stripe_df,
                              aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                              fill = stripe_df$fill, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = id))
  if (!is.null(stripe_layer)) p <- p + stripe_layer
  p +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = .data[[lwr_col]], ymax = .data[[upr_col]],
                      color = .cov_grp, alpha = .cov_grp), width = 0.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(covered = panel_color, missed = "gray70"),
                       guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(covered = 0.80, missed = 0.30),
                       guide = "none") +
    ##### PATCH 6: black-dot midpoint geom_point removed
    geom_point(aes(y = upmc.dead_60), color = "red2", size = 0.6, shape = 4, stroke = 0.7) +
    ##### Request-3: panel title carries CP and (when supplied) AL, so both
    ##### metrics live on the plot and the separate CP/AL summary table is
    ##### unnecessary.
    labs(title = {
           .cp <- paste0("CP ", formatC(cov_for_title, format = "f", digits = 3))
           if (!is.null(al_full)) {
             paste0(method_label, "  (", .cp,
                    ", AL ", formatC(al_full, format = "f", digits = 3), ")")
           } else {
             paste0(method_label, "  (", .cp, ")")
           }
         },
         x = "Ranked patients (subsample)", y = "60-day mortality") +
    ylim(-0.10, 1.02) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
}

```


## Clipping diagnostic (Option 2)

Conformal intervals are constructed on the score scale and can extend
below 0 or above 1, even though the outcome `dead_60` is binary. We adopt
the following convention: the displayed plot intervals are clipped to
$[0, 1]$; **average length is reported on these $[0,1]$-clipped intervals**
(the actual informative width, since the part of an interval below 0 or
above 1 carries no information for a probability/binary outcome and would
otherwise inflate the reported length); and **coverage is computed on the
raw (unclipped) intervals**. Clipping to $[0,1]$ cannot change whether the
binary points 0 or 1 fall inside an interval, so coverage is identical
whether measured on raw or clipped intervals --- the two reporting choices
are mutually consistent. The chunk below quantifies how often clipping
changes the interval.

```{r clipping-diagnostic}
##### CLEANUP: clipping diagnostic for Option 2.
##### Reports, per method, how many intervals would have been altered by
##### clipping, average length pre/post clipping, and coverage pre/post.
.diag <- function(lwr, upr, y) {
  n <- length(lwr)
  ok <- !is.na(lwr) & !is.na(upr)
  lwr <- lwr[ok]; upr <- upr[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  clipped <- lwr < 0 | upr > 1
  len_raw <- upr - lwr
  lwr_c <- pmin(1, pmax(0, lwr))
  upr_c <- pmin(1, pmax(0, upr))
  len_clp <- upr_c - lwr_c
  cov_raw <- mean(lwr   <= y & upr   >= y)
  cov_clp <- mean(lwr_c <= y & upr_c >= y)
  data.frame(
    n               = n,
    n_with_clipping = sum(clipped),
    pct_clipped     = round(100 * mean(clipped), 1),
    avg_len_raw     = round(mean(len_raw), 3),
    avg_len_clipped = round(mean(len_clp), 3),
    coverage_raw    = round(cov_raw, 3),
    coverage_clipped= round(cov_clp, 3)
  )
}
.y <- upmcIntv_blockA_W$upmc.dead_60
diag_tbl <- rbind(
  cbind(method = "tCOPP-W",       .diag(upmcIntv_blockA_W$out_lefts_sofa,    upmcIntv_blockA_W$out_rights_sofa,    .y)),
  cbind(method = "tCOPP-EIF(I)",  .diag(upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$out_lefts_sofa, upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$out_rights_sofa, .y)),
  cbind(method = "tCOPP-EIF(M)",  .diag(upmcIntv_blockB$out_lefts_sofa,      upmcIntv_blockB$out_rights_sofa,      .y)),
  cbind(method = "tCOPP-EIF(P)",  .diag(upmcIntv_blockB$out_lefts_pool_sofa, upmcIntv_blockB$out_rights_pool_sofa, .y))
)
print(diag_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
```

## mu_hat calibration diagnostic (Patch 7.2)

A general sanity check on the conditional-mean predictions used as the
midpoint of each interval. For each method, it prints the distribution
of mu_hat (per-patient point estimate) and a coarse calibration table
(predicted-bin x observed-mean). The model used in the active code
path is the ridge regression in the score-functions chunk; mu_hat should
spread across the interior, roughly tracking the observed mortality
rate (~0.18 on the UPMC sample). If mu_hat is bunched at 0 or 1, that
would indicate fitted probabilities have collapsed and the outcome
model needs more regularization or more training data.

```{r mu-hat-calibration}
##### PATCH 7.2: mu_hat calibration diagnostic (retained from 7.1)
.mu_summary <- function(mu, y, label) {
  ok <- !is.na(mu)
  mu <- mu[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  qs <- quantile(mu, c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95))
  cat(sprintf("\n%s (n=%d): mean=%.3f, sd=%.3f, q05=%.3f, q25=%.3f, q50=%.3f, q75=%.3f, q95=%.3f\n",
              label, length(mu), mean(mu), sd(mu),
              qs[1], qs[2], qs[3], qs[4], qs[5]))
  cat(sprintf("  observed outcome mean = %.3f; predicted mean = %.3f (gap = %+.3f)\n",
              mean(y), mean(mu), mean(mu) - mean(y)))
  # Coarse calibration table: 5 bins of predicted probability
  brks <- unique(quantile(mu, seq(0, 1, by = 0.2), na.rm = TRUE))
  if (length(brks) >= 3) {
    bin <- cut(mu, breaks = brks, include.lowest = TRUE)
    tbl <- data.frame(
      bin       = levels(bin),
      n         = as.numeric(table(bin)),
      pred_mean = round(tapply(mu, bin, mean),  3),
      obs_mean  = round(tapply(y,  bin, mean),  3)
    )
    cat("  calibration (predicted-bin x observed):\n")
    print(tbl, row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
.mu_summary(upmcIntv_blockA_W$mu_hat_sofa,    upmc$dead_60, "tCOPP-W   ")
.mu_summary(upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$mu_hat_sofa, upmc$dead_60, "tCOPP-EIF(I)")
.mu_summary(upmcIntv_blockB$mu_hat_sofa,      upmc$dead_60, "tCOPP-EIF(M/P)")
```

```{r plot-combined-2x2-const, fig.width=12, fig.height=9}
  W_lwr    = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockA_W$out_lefts_egdt)),
  W_lwr_raw = upmcIntv_blockA_W$out_lefts_egdt,
  W_upr    = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockA_W$out_rights_egdt)),
  W_upr_raw = upmcIntv_blockA_W$out_rights_egdt,
  W_mu     = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockA_W$mu_hat_egdt)),

  # tCOPP-EIF(I) under pi_e = 1
  EIFI_lwr = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$out_lefts_egdt)),
  EIFI_lwr_raw = upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$out_lefts_egdt,
  EIFI_upr = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$out_rights_egdt)),
  EIFI_upr_raw = upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$out_rights_egdt,
  EIFI_mu  = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockA_EIFI$mu_hat_egdt)),

  # tCOPP-EIF(M) under pi_e = 1
  EIFM_lwr = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockB$out_lefts_egdt)),
  EIFM_lwr_raw = upmcIntv_blockB$out_lefts_egdt,
  EIFM_upr = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockB$out_rights_egdt)),
  EIFM_upr_raw = upmcIntv_blockB$out_rights_egdt,
  EIFM_mu  = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockB$mu_hat_egdt)),

  # tCOPP-EIF(P) under pi_e = 1
  EIFP_lwr = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockB$out_lefts_pool_egdt)),
  EIFP_lwr_raw = upmcIntv_blockB$out_lefts_pool_egdt,
  EIFP_upr = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockB$out_rights_pool_egdt)),
  EIFP_upr_raw = upmcIntv_blockB$out_rights_pool_egdt,
  EIFP_mu  = pmin(1, pmax(0, upmcIntv_blockB$mu_hat_egdt))
  ##### No SOFA stripe here: the constant policy does NOT depend on SOFA, so a
  ##### severity stripe would only confuse readers (see the severity-adaptive
  ##### figure for the stripe, where the policy actually uses SOFA).
)

plot_subsample_const <- plotdat_const[
  order(plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60)[seq(1, nrow(plotdat_const), by = 30)], ]

##### Full-population coverage for the panel titles (matches summary table)
cov_full_const_W    <- mean(plotdat_const$W_lwr_raw    <= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60 & plotdat_const$W_upr_raw    >= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60, na.rm = TRUE)
cov_full_const_EIFI <- mean(plotdat_const$EIFI_lwr_raw <= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60 & plotdat_const$EIFI_upr_raw >= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60, na.rm = TRUE)
cov_full_const_EIFM <- mean(plotdat_const$EIFM_lwr_raw <= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60 & plotdat_const$EIFM_upr_raw >= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60, na.rm = TRUE)
cov_full_const_EIFP <- mean(plotdat_const$EIFP_lwr_raw <= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60 & plotdat_const$EIFP_upr_raw >= plotdat_const$upmc.dead_60, na.rm = TRUE)

##### Request-3: full-population AVERAGE LENGTH (AL) per method on the
##### [0,1]-clipped intervals, mirroring the SOFA chunk. Passed to make_panel so
##### CP and AL both appear in each panel title (no separate summary table).
al_full_const_W    <- mean(plotdat_const$W_upr    - plotdat_const$W_lwr,    na.rm = TRUE)
al_full_const_EIFI <- mean(plotdat_const$EIFI_upr - plotdat_const$EIFI_lwr, na.rm = TRUE)
al_full_const_EIFM <- mean(plotdat_const$EIFM_upr - plotdat_const$EIFM_lwr, na.rm = TRUE)
al_full_const_EIFP <- mean(plotdat_const$EIFP_upr - plotdat_const$EIFP_lwr, na.rm = TRUE)

##### Request-1: as in the SOFA figure, tCOPP-EIF(P) is the pooled oracle (title
##### tagged "(oracle)") kept only as the bottom-right reference against the
##### federated multi-source tCOPP-EIF(M); the top row is the two single-source
##### proposed methods.
c1 <- make_panel(plot_subsample_const, "W_lwr",    "W_upr",    "W_mu",    "tCOPP-W",               "limegreen",   cov_full = cov_full_const_W,    lwr_raw_col = "W_lwr_raw",    upr_raw_col = "W_upr_raw",    al_full = al_full_const_W)
c2 <- make_panel(plot_subsample_const, "EIFI_lwr", "EIFI_upr", "EIFI_mu", "tCOPP-EIF(I)",          "deepskyblue", cov_full = cov_full_const_EIFI, lwr_raw_col = "EIFI_lwr_raw", upr_raw_col = "EIFI_upr_raw", al_full = al_full_const_EIFI)
c3 <- make_panel(plot_subsample_const, "EIFM_lwr", "EIFM_upr", "EIFM_mu", "tCOPP-EIF(M)",          "darkorange",  cov_full = cov_full_const_EIFM, lwr_raw_col = "EIFM_lwr_raw", upr_raw_col = "EIFM_upr_raw", al_full = al_full_const_EIFM)
c4 <- make_panel(plot_subsample_const, "EIFP_lwr", "EIFP_upr", "EIFP_mu", "tCOPP-EIF(P) (oracle)", "purple3",     cov_full = cov_full_const_EIFP, lwr_raw_col = "EIFP_lwr_raw", upr_raw_col = "EIFP_upr_raw", al_full = al_full_const_EIFP)

((c1 | c2) / (c3 | c4)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    caption = paste(
  
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    theme = theme(plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
                  plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8))
  )

##### Request-3: standalone CP/AL summary table removed; CP and AL are in the
##### panel titles above. (Coverage-by-outcome diagnostic below is retained.)
```













# Sensitivity analysis (opt-in)

The primary analysis above uses the smooth severity-adaptive evaluation
policy $\pi_e(\text{EGDT}\mid X) = \mathrm{expit}\{\beta(\text{SOFA}-m)/s\}$
(`Deta_smooth`, defined in the `patch6-define-policy` chunk; tune `beta_sofa`).

For sensitivity, the legacy all-EGDT and all-UC policies remain available
as `Deta_egdt` and `Deta_uc` (defined in the `patch4-define-policy` chunk
near the top of this file). Each analysis block also has the original
"second half" code preserved inside `if (FALSE) { ... }` — this is the
all-UC run from the legacy code. To execute a sensitivity analysis,
**three steps**:

1. **Pick a policy** (`Deta_egdt` or `Deta_uc`) and a block (A-tCOPP-W,
   A-tCOPP-EIF(I), or B).
2. **Modify the relevant analysis chunk** by changing
   `Deta <- Deta_smooth` to `Deta <- Deta_egdt` (or `Deta_uc`), re-run that
   block, then snapshot the result with a sensitivity-suffixed name like
   `upmcIntv_blockB_egdt <- upmcIntv`.
3. **Plot** with a copy of the relevant plot chunk that swaps
   `upmcIntv_blockB` for `upmcIntv_blockB_egdt`.

This is intentionally manual to avoid re-running the slow analyses by
default. A scripted version would be a useful future addition (Patch 5).

```{r sensitivity-stub, eval=FALSE}
##### EXAMPLE: Sensitivity run skeleton.
##### To execute, set eval=TRUE on this chunk AND re-run all analysis blocks
##### above with Deta_smooth replaced by your chosen sensitivity policy.

# Step 1: Pick policy
sensitivity_Deta <- Deta_egdt   # or Deta_uc

# Step 2: Re-run an analysis block with this Deta. Easiest way: temporarily
# alias Deta_smooth to your sensitivity policy, then re-execute the block.
Deta_smooth_BACKUP <- Deta_smooth
Deta_smooth      <- sensitivity_Deta

# (Re-run analysis chunks here — interactive; or in a knit, use child documents.)

# Step 3: Snapshot with a sensitivity-suffixed name
# upmcIntv_blockB_egdt <- upmcIntv

# Step 4: Restore primary
Deta_smooth <- Deta_smooth_BACKUP
```
